subject: physics

items.q: What does it mean for an energy resource to be 'renewable'?
items.correct: It is replenished on a human timescale and won't run out — though it may still have some environmental impact.
items.misconception: Renewable means it causes no environmental harm at all.
items.random_wrong: Renewable just means it is cheaper than fossil fuels.
items.why: Renewable refers to replenishment, not zero impact: biofuels release CO2, hydro floods land. Non-renewables (coal, oil, gas, uranium) run out.

items.q: What happens to energy when an electrical device runs?
items.correct: It is transferred and dissipated (often as heat to the surroundings) — never destroyed.
items.misconception: It is used up and no longer exists once the device has worked.
items.random_wrong: It is created from nothing by the device.
items.why: Conservation of energy: the total stays constant. 'Wasted' energy spreads out as thermal energy to the surroundings, it is not lost.

items.q: Is nuclear power a renewable or non-renewable resource?
items.correct: Non-renewable — its uranium fuel is finite and will run out.
items.misconception: Renewable, because it doesn't burn fossil fuels.
items.random_wrong: Renewable, because the reaction never stops on its own.
items.why: Although nuclear emits little CO2, the uranium fuel is a limited resource, so it is classed as non-renewable.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics (4PH1) specification; Energy Resources & Energy Transfers
